questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were multiple aspects that were crucial for choosing my study destination. I wanted to study at a university with a high academic level and also a university with a big campus to experience that kind of study environment. I also wanted to live in a city with diverse cultures, and Toronto was a perfect choice. Lastly, I wanted to study at a university that offered courses that suited my academic profile and would help me in my future studies.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The reason for not choosing a higher is due to the fact that Covid-19 was still affecting social life and also the accessibility at the campus during the first two months of my study abroad.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to find all the important information from the University of Copenhagen. The websites for studying abroad are very good. The websites from the University of Toronto were a bit harder to navigate, but it was also fairly easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any assistance from the University of Toronto other than some e-mails with information about the study and social groups. We had to figure almost everything out by ourselves, which was done by asking other exchange students. They could have made an exchange group with some introduction for those who want to join.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Maybe the little assistance was due to Covid-19, which did not allow exchange students to meet at the campus during the first months.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It wasn't easy to find housing. There are not so many student housing opportunities. I found two student houses with reasonable prices, but they were completely full even 4 months before the semester started. I found my housing on a Facebook page for renting rooms in Toronto.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: For future exchange students going to Toronto I would recommend going for the two student housing opportunities called "Tartu" and "Harrington housing". If these are not possible then be very careful when finding a room through Facebook. I would recommend having a video call with the host and be sure that its not some fraud.

Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I received the necessary e-mails for registration, which were very intuitive and made the process easy. I would recommend doing it as soon as possible as you have to do an online to obtain your student card, and the number of these meetings is limited. For registration for courses we received multiple e-mails with the different rounds of registration, which helped a lot.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: E-mails with the necessary information.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very successful. I got all the classes that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find the courses you want very early in the process as the first round of registration is very early.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very high academic level and sometimes too much work.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the level very high. I had to study a lot, but it was also what I wanted to challenge myself.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different. At the University of Toronto, they focused a lot on midterm exams. So even 2 weeks into the course we had midterm exams that affected our final grades. At UCPH the grading of courses is based on the final exam at the end of the semester. So, if you want a good grade at the University of Toronto you have to work and study throughout the whole semester where it at UCPH was based on the final exam.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
PCL481H1 The Molecular and Biochemical Basis of Toxicology
PHC331H1 Establishing the Bioequivalence of Pharmaceutical Products
PHC401H1 Drug Transport Across Biological Membranes
PHC420H1 The Science of Pharmacotherapy
PHC421H1 Biomolecular Interactions and Thermodynamics I

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: PHC401H1 Drug Transport Across Biological Membranes and PHC421H1 Biomolecular Interactions and Thermodynamics I. These two courses focused very much on specific topics and I would very much recommend these if you are interested in these topics.

Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of gyms and sport teams you could join.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You could join every kind of sport team and also join for tournaments even if your exchange eas only one semester.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the intramurals (sport tournament).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to games (basketball, ice hockey etc.) and eat out (very good and diverse).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I found it hard to socialize with local students. They were very academic-oriented and did not do much else than studying.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The partying culture at the campus was inexisting, which is very different compared to Copenhagen.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The academic level.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Join some sports teams, it's where you find the most friends. 
Go to the libraries on the campus, also a place to find friends. 
Study most in the beginning of the semester, so you can have more time for fun in the end.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be open from the beginning and join as many things as possible with other exchange students.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Finding very good friends and spending time with them and also the final grades.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Some of the courses were very intimidating in the beginning. In one course we were 6 students, so challenging and different to what I was used to.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
